scope.title: Frame the research question
scope.prompt: Help me frame this pharmacoeconomic or HEOR decision problem. Start from what I provide and confirm the population, intervention, comparator, outcomes, perspective, time horizon, and intended decision use. Ask only for information that would materially change the study.

evidence.title: Find and organize evidence
evidence.prompt: Help me find and organize the evidence needed for this pharmacoeconomic study. First clarify the decision problem and evidence gaps, then identify useful local sources, searches that may be needed, provenance, and limitations. Before any network access, show the exact query and fields that would leave this computer.

model.title: Design or review a model
model.prompt: Help me design or review this health economic model. Start from the decision problem and examine model structure, parameter evidence, key assumptions, uncertainty, and validation requirements. Keep calculation errors separate from issues that require researcher judgment.

deliverable.title: Analyze data or prepare a briefing
deliverable.prompt: Help me with this pharmacoeconomic or HEOR task. I can provide data, a model, a report, or briefing requirements. First inventory the available materials and expected deliverable, then propose a reviewable analysis or production path.

firstRun.title: Before you begin
firstRun.body: Under your direction, AI4HEOR can organize evidence, carry out analyses, and check results. You review the study plan, key assumptions, evidence choices, and use of the conclusions.

local.title: Local by default
local.body: Projects and research files stay on this device unless you explicitly use an external service.

provider.title: Your choice of model
provider.body: Choose any supported provider or local endpoint. Nothing is sent until you send a research request.

approval.title: Actions remain reviewable
approval.body: The default approval mode asks before deletion, installation, network, remote, or privileged actions.

human.title: You review key research decisions
human.body: Model output remains a working draft. You review the study plan, key assumptions, evidence choices, and use of the conclusions.

starters.heading: What HEOR question should we work on?
starters.subheading: Describe your pharmacoeconomic question — or begin with a researcher-led workflow.

design.title: Start a pharmacoeconomic study
design.description: Define the decision problem, conceptual model, evidence needs, and Human review points.
design.prompt: Help me start a researcher-led pharmacoeconomic or HEOR study. Use $heor-workbench and $heor-model-design. First ask concise questions about the population, intervention, comparators, outcomes, perspective, jurisdiction, time horizon, decision context, available evidence, and intended use. Then prepare reviewable local artifacts and an explicit plan. Do not choose scientific methods, assumptions, evidence, thresholds, or approvals for the human researcher.

analyze.title: Analyze my HEOR evidence or data
analyze.description: Inventory local evidence and data, clarify the estimand, then propose an auditable analysis.
analyze.prompt: Help me analyze the HEOR evidence or data in this project. Use $heor-workbench to inventory relevant local files first, identify what each file can and cannot support, and ask me to confirm the decision question, estimand, population, comparator, outcomes, and method before execution. Keep computation deterministic where supported, preserve provenance, and stop at Human-in-the-loop method and interpretation decisions.

audit.title: Audit an HEOR model or report
audit.description: Check methods, inputs, model-result bindings, reporting, limitations, and reproducibility.
audit.prompt: Audit the current HEOR model, analysis, or report using the relevant AI4HEOR validation, reporting, reproducibility, and traceability Skills. Ask me which artifact graph to review if it is ambiguous. Separate deterministic defects from scientific judgments, bind every finding to exact local evidence, and never create Human approval or claim methodological validity.

example-cea.title: Explore an example: cost-effectiveness analysis
example-cea.description: Synthetic two-strategy cohort inputs for an auditable cost-utility workflow.
example-cea.prompt: Use $heor-workbench to explore the synthetic demonstration files under heor-cost-effectiveness/. Treat every number as a proposed teaching assumption, not clinical or economic evidence. Explain the decision problem, review the three-state cohort structure, reproduce the base-case cost and QALY calculation with deterministic code, run one transparent sensitivity check, and prepare a local report with limitations and Human review points. Do not create approvals or reimbursement conclusions.
